complexity_added: MODERATE: added a second cost measurement (Gate 2: true 1-day-hold daily-rebalance cost drag) because the existing walk-forward gate carries positions through the 84-day test window and does not reflect full daily-rebalance costs; plus a complete independent verifier covering both gates.
methodology_notes: The existing gate's per-fold medians are cost-insensitive by construction: walk-forward folds carry the position through the 84-bar test window, so only fills executed inside the test window pay costs; Gate 2 was added to measure the stated 1-day-hold daily-rebalance strategy's true cost drag.

Gate 1 null medians were reproduced exactly by the verifier using the framework's own noise_benchmark (same deterministic seed derivation), so the few verdict flips between cost configs (e.g. JPM lookback-5 REGIME_DEPENDENT->REGIME_STABLE under realistic/heavy) are pure null-dispersion effects, not candidate changes.
Cost values are on a $1M constant-dollar book at target_exposure 1.0; AAPL representative mean round-trip cost = $3,174/day (0.3174% of capital); costs scale with share price and position size.

question: Does the short-horizon momentum edge survive conservative transaction-cost stress on the collected real-data universe?
research_result: VERIFIED_NEGATIVE_RESULT: short-horizon momentum (lookback 3/5/10) is not cost-robust under the repository's existing realistic cost model for the 1-day-hold daily-rebalance strategy; conservative round-trip transaction costs exceed the gross edge by ~3x and produce a negative net edge across all three lookbacks.
uncertainty_reduced: The decision-relevant cost-robustness question is now answered with verified numbers: conservative round-trip costs (~0.32%/day) exceed the gross short-horizon momentum edge (~0.11%/day) by ~3x, so the edge is erased and reversed at realistic costs (net -0.195%/day median; ~-49%/yr log) and worse at 2x (net -0.47%/day).
